examples.en: Making money by lying is immoral.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 광고는 부도덕하다고 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The company's ad was criticized as unethical.

examples.ko: 시험에서 답을 훔쳐보는 것은 부도덕한 행동이에요.
examples.en: Peeking at answers on a test is immoral behavior.

examples.ko: 그는 부도덕하게 번 돈을 모두 돌려줬어요.
examples.en: He gave back all the money he had earned unethically.
He deeply regretted his immoral past.

examples.ko: 책임을 남에게 넘기는 건 부도덕해 보여요.
examples.en: Passing the blame to others looks unethical.

explain: 반대말은 '도덕적이다'예요. 강하게 비난하는 느낌이라서 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 나와요. 가벼운 잘못에는 '나쁘다', '잘못이다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The opposite is 도덕적이다. It carries strong criticism, so it shows up in news and writing more than in everyday talk. For small mistakes, 나쁘다 or 잘못이다 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 사람이 많은 지하철에서는 소매치기를 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should watch out for pickpockets on a crowded subway.
A pickpocket took my wallet at the market.
I saw news that the police caught a pickpocket.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 소매치기 조심하라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Before the trip, I was told to beware of pickpockets.

examples.ko: 저는 어제 버스 정류장에서 소매치기를 당할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got pickpocketed at the bus stop yesterday.

examples.ko: 소매치기가 많은 곳에서는 가방을 앞으로 메요.
examples.en: In places with many pickpockets, I wear my bag in front.

explain: 피해를 입었을 때는 '소매치기를 당하다'라고 하고, 소매치기를 하는 사람도 소매치기라고 불러요. '도둑'은 훔치는 사람 전체를 부르고, 소매치기는 사람이 많은 곳에서 몰래 가져가는 도둑이에요.
explain_en: When you are the victim, you say 소매치기를 당하다, and the thief is also called 소매치기. 도둑 covers any thief, while 소매치기 is one who quietly takes things in crowded places.

examples.en: That man picked pockets on the subway yesterday.
He got caught by the police while picking pockets at the market.

examples.ko: 소매치기하는 사람은 보통 눈에 잘 안 띄어요.
examples.en: People who pick pockets usually don't stand out.

examples.ko: 저를 소매치기한 사람은 아직 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: They still haven't found the person who picked my pocket.

examples.ko: 그는 어렸을 때 소매치기하며 살았다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he lived by picking pockets when he was young.
The culprit picked the tourist's wallet and ran away.

explain: 피해자 입장에서는 '소매치기를 당하다'가 자연스러워요. '소매치기하다'는 저지른 사람을 말할 때 써요. 훔치는 일 전체는 '훔치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: From the victim's side, 소매치기를 당하다 is the natural phrase. 소매치기하다 is used about the person who did it. Stealing in general is 훔치다.

examples.en: A baby's face has soft fuzz.

examples.ko: 복숭아 껍질에 솜털이 많이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a lot of fuzz on the peach skin.

examples.ko: 솜털 같은 구름이 하늘에 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Fluffy clouds are floating in the sky.
Because of the cold, the fine hair on my arm stood up.
Chicks are covered in yellow down.

examples.ko: 그는 아직 수염 대신 솜털만 나 있어요.
examples.en: He still has only peach fuzz instead of a beard.

explain: 아기, 병아리, 복숭아처럼 아주 가늘고 부드러운 털에 써요. 굵고 진한 '털'과 달리 연한 느낌이에요. 소름이 돋을 때 서는 것도 솜털이에요.
explain_en: It is used for very thin, soft hair on babies, chicks, or peaches. Unlike thick, dark 털, it feels light and faint. The hair that stands up when you get goosebumps is also 솜털.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 파출소에는 여경이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two policewomen at our neighborhood police box.
A policewoman helped me when I got lost.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 여경이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to be a policewoman since I was little.

examples.ko: 여경 채용 시험에 지원한 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who applied for the policewoman hiring exam.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 여경이 범인을 쫓는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene in a drama where a policewoman chases a criminal.
I asked a policewoman for directions at the event.

explain: 남자 경찰은 보통 그냥 '경찰'이라고 하고, 여자 경찰을 따로 말할 때 '여경'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '경찰관님'을 써요. 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Male officers are usually just called 경찰, and 여경 is used when you single out a woman officer. When addressing one directly, you use 경찰관님. You see 여경 often in news and articles.

examples.en: Mhm, I'll go together with you tomorrow too.
Are you very hungry? Mhm, a little hungry.
Uh-huh, I heard that story too.

examples.ko: 친구가 물었을 때 으응 하고 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: When my friend asked, I said mhm and nodded.
Mhm, it's okay. Don't worry.

examples.ko: 아이가 졸린 얼굴로 으응 하고 대답했어요.
examples.en: The child answered 'mhm' with a sleepy face.

explain: '응'을 길게 끌어서 부드럽거나 졸린 느낌으로 대답하는 말이에요. 친구나 가족처럼 가까운 사이에서 써요. 윗사람에게는 '네'나 '예'를 써야 해요.
explain_en: It is a drawn-out version of 응 that sounds soft or sleepy. Use it only with close friends or family. To someone older or senior, say 네 or 예 instead.

examples.en: I have a lot of work these days, so I work on weekends too.
The man said he is worried because there is no work.
I brought work home and did it until late at night.
I'm looking for new work.
When it rains, the construction site jobs decrease.

examples.ko: 저는 방학 동안 작은 일거리를 구했어요.
examples.en: I found a small job during vacation.

explain: '일'보다 구체적으로 해야 할 작업이나 돈을 벌 수 있는 일감을 말할 때 써요. '일거리가 많다/없다', '일거리를 찾다'처럼 써요. '직업'은 오래 하는 일이고, 일거리는 그때그때 생기는 일이에요.
explain_en: It is more concrete than 일: tasks waiting to be done or work you can earn money from. It goes with phrases like 일거리가 많다/없다 and 일거리를 찾다. A 직업 is a long-term occupation, while 일거리 is work that comes up from time to time.

en: squeeze out; wring out; rack (one's brain)

examples.ko: 치약을 끝까지 짜낸 다음에 새것을 샀어요.
examples.en: I squeezed out the toothpaste to the end and then bought a new one.
Squeeze the lemon and put it in the water.
I wring the water out of the wet clothes.
I stayed up all night squeezing out ideas.

examples.ko: 회의에서 좋은 방법을 짜내 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: At the meeting, they said let's come up with a good method.
I'm worried because there's no way to scrape money together.

explain: '짜다'는 눌러서 물이나 내용물을 나오게 하는 말이고, '짜내다'는 끝까지 힘을 줘서 밖으로 빼내는 느낌이 더 강해요. 아이디어나 돈처럼 어렵게 만들어 낼 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I racked my brain to solve the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 열심히 생각해서 방법을 찾으려고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you think very hard to find a way.

explain_en: 짜다 means pressing to get liquid or contents out; 짜내다 feels stronger, as if you push until it all comes out. It is also used for producing things with effort, like ideas or money.

examples.en: My younger sibling is still immature and only plays pranks.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 철없는 말을 자주 해요.
examples.en: That child often says thoughtless things.
I sometimes miss my carefree, naive days.

examples.ko: 스무 살인데 너무 철없이 행동한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm twenty, but I think I acted too childishly.
My friends tease me for being immature.
I was immature. I'm really sorry.

explain: '철이 없다'와 같은 말이고, 반대말은 '철들다'예요. 나이에 맞지 않게 생각이 어린 사람에게 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 흉보는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is the same as 철이 없다, and the opposite is 철들다. It is used for someone whose thinking is younger than their age. Said about an adult, it sounds like strong criticism.

examples.en: I saw a mirror made of bronze at the museum.

examples.ko: 광장 한가운데에 청동 동상이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A bronze statue stands in the middle of the square.
Bronze is made by mixing copper and tin.
A bronze knife was found in the tomb.

examples.ko: 이 종은 청동이라서 소리가 오래 울려요.
examples.en: This bell is bronze, so the sound rings for a long time.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에는 오래된 청동 그릇이 있어요.
examples.en: My grandmother's house has an old bronze bowl.

explain: 올림픽 3등 상은 '동메달'이라고 하고 '청동 메달'이라고는 잘 안 해요. 청동은 '청동기 시대', '청동 거울', '청동상'처럼 역사 이야기와 유물·조각 이름에 주로 써요.
explain_en: For the Olympic third place, people say 동메달, not 청동 메달. 청동 mostly appears in history topics and names of relics and statues, such as 청동기 시대, 청동 거울, and 청동상.

examples.en: My father's car still has a cassette player.
My grandmother listens to old songs on a cassette player.
I don't know where the cassette tape went.

examples.ko: 중학교 때 카세트로 영어 듣기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: In middle school, I practiced English listening with a cassette player.

examples.ko: 이 카세트는 고장 나서 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: This cassette player is broken and makes no sound.
These days, shops that sell cassettes are rare.

explain: '카세트 테이프'라고 해서 테이프 자체를 말하기도 하고, 테이프를 트는 기계를 말하기도 해요. 요즘은 스마트폰으로 음악을 들어서 옛날 이야기를 할 때 많이 나와요. 기계는 '카세트 플레이어'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It can mean the tape itself, called 카세트 테이프, or the machine that plays it. Since people now listen to music on smartphones, it comes up mostly when talking about the past. The machine can also be called 카세트 플레이어.

examples.en: This storm is really destructive.
People were shocked by the earthquake's destructive power.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 공을 파괴력 있게 차요.
examples.en: That player kicks the ball with real force.
The impact of a rumor is much bigger than you think.

examples.ko: 새 기술이 시장에서 큰 파괴력을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The new technology showed great disruptive power in the market.
It was a weak typhoon, so the damage was small.

explain: 무기나 태풍처럼 부수는 힘에 쓰고, 스포츠나 소문처럼 상대를 크게 흔드는 힘에도 써요. 비슷한 '위력'은 좋은 일에도 쓰지만 '파괴력'은 부수고 흔드는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used for smashing power like weapons or typhoons, and also for strong influence such as in sports or rumors. The similar 위력 can describe good things too, while 파괴력 has a feel of breaking and shaking things.

examples.en: I saw a sea horse for the first time at the aquarium.
The sea horse is holding onto seaweed with its tail.

examples.ko: 아이가 해마 모양 인형을 갖고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: The child wanted a sea horse-shaped doll.
My friend said the sea horse looks like a horse.
I want to swim with sea horses in the ocean.

examples.ko: 해마의 수컷이 새끼를 낳는다는 사실을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned that the male sea horse gives birth to the young.

explain: 뇌에서 기억을 맡는 부분도 '해마'라고 불러서 같은 소리의 말이에요. 문장 속 내용을 보면 동물인지 뇌인지 알 수 있어요. 동물 해마는 머리 모양이 말을 닮아서 이름에 '마'(말)가 들어가요.
explain_en: The part of the brain that handles memory is also called 해마, so the same word has two meanings. The context tells you whether it is the animal or the brain. The animal has 마, meaning horse, in its name because its head looks like a horse.

examples.en: When the Earth gets warmer, sea levels rise.
The sun is rising above the sea surface.
The height of the sea surface differs slightly from sea to sea.
The news said rising sea levels are a problem.
The boat moves slowly close to the sea surface.

examples.ko: 섬이 해수면보다 낮아서 홍수가 자주 나요.
examples.en: The island is lower than sea level, so floods happen often.

explain: 산 높이를 말할 때는 '해발 1,000미터'처럼 '해발'을 쓰고, 바닷물의 높이 변화를 말할 때는 '해수면'을 써요. 뉴스에서 '해수면 상승'이라는 말로 자주 들어요.
explain_en: For the height of a mountain, Korean says 해발 1,000미터. For changes in the height of the sea, it uses 해수면. You hear it often in the news as 해수면 상승.

examples.en: A stork was standing in the rice field.
A stork has very long legs and a long beak.
I watched a stork family at the zoo.

examples.ko: 황새는 높은 나무 위에 커다란 둥지를 지어요.
examples.en: A stork builds a big nest high in a tree.
The children drew a stork in a picture.
I looked for a bird with long legs like a stork.

explain: '황새', '두루미', '백로'는 모두 다리가 긴 큰 새라서 헷갈려요. 황새는 몸이 크고 흰색에 날개 끝이 검고, 백로는 더 작고 하얗고, 두루미는 정수리가 빨개요.
explain_en: 황새, 두루미, and 백로 are all large long-legged birds, so they get confused. 황새 is big and white with black wing tips, 백로 is smaller and all white, and 두루미 has a red patch on top of its head.

examples.en: I'll finish my homework quickly and go out to play.
I'm hungry, so I'll eat dinner quickly and head out.
The time flew by.
I got the cleaning done in a flash and rested.
I'll be right back, so please wait.
I washed up quickly in the morning and left home.

explain: '빨리'보다 입말에 가깝고, 일을 가볍게 서둘러 끝내는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 '얼른'은 지금 바로 하라고 재촉할 때도 많이 써요. 격식 있는 글이나 윗사람에게는 '빨리'가 더 안전해요.
explain_en: It is closer to spoken language than 빨리 and feels like getting something done lightly and fast. The similar 얼른 is also often used to urge someone to do something right now. In formal writing or with elders, 빨리 is safer.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 코를 후비는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Picking your nose in front of people is not polite.
My ear hurt while I was digging in it.

examples.ko: 아이가 모래를 손으로 후벼 파고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is digging into the sand with his hands.
I picked between my teeth with a toothpick.
When I rummaged in my pocket, a coin came out.
Don't pick at the wound; just leave it.

explain: 손가락이나 뾰족한 도구로 좁은 곳 안쪽을 긁어내듯 건드릴 때 써요. '코를 후비다', '귀를 후비다'로 가장 많이 쓰여요. '파다'는 땅을 팔 때도 쓰지만, '후비다'는 작은 구멍 안쪽을 건드리는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes poking or scraping inside a narrow spot with a finger or a pointed tool. Its most common use is 코를 후비다 and 귀를 후비다. 파다 can mean digging the ground, while 후비다 feels like touching the inside of a small hole.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에는 엄마가 갈치구이를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Tonight Mom made grilled hairtail for me.
I tried braised hairtail in Jeju.

examples.ko: 시장에서 싱싱한 갈치 세 마리를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought three fresh hairtail at the market.
A hairtail has a long body and shines silver.
Hairtail was expensive, so I bought mackerel instead.

examples.ko: 갈치의 살은 부드러워서 아이도 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Hairtail meat is soft, so even kids eat it well.

explain: '고등어'와 함께 한국 식탁에서 자주 만나는 생선이에요. 구이나 조림으로 많이 먹고, 제주도 갈치가 유명해요. 생선은 '마리'로 세요.
explain_en: Along with 고등어, it is a fish often seen on Korean tables. It is commonly eaten grilled or braised, and Jeju hairtail is famous. Fish are counted with 마리.

examples.en: We installed a smoke detector at our house.
The detector went off, so everyone went outside.

examples.ko: 이 감지기는 움직임이 있으면 불이 켜져요.
examples.en: This sensor turns on the light when there is movement.

examples.ko: 문 앞 감지기에 손을 대면 문이 열려요.
examples.en: If you put your hand on the sensor by the door, it opens.
I check whether the gas detector is on.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 감지기로 사람이 있는지 확인해요.
examples.en: This building uses sensors to check whether anyone is there.

explain: '센서'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '센서'를 더 흔하게 쓰고, '감지기'는 '화재 감지기', '연기 감지기', '움직임 감지기'처럼 안전 장치 이름에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as 센서. In daily life 센서 is more common, while 감지기 appears often in safety device names such as 화재 감지기 and 연기 감지기.

examples.ko: 대장장이는 불에 쇠를 달궈서 칼을 만들어요.
examples.en: A blacksmith heats iron in a fire to make knives.

examples.ko: 옛날 마을에는 대장장이가 한 명씩 있었어요.
examples.en: In old times, each village had a blacksmith.
My father dreamed of being a blacksmith as a child.
The sound of the blacksmith's hammer rang through the village.

examples.ko: 대장장이에게 낫을 새로 만들어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the blacksmith to make a new sickle.

examples.ko: 요즘에도 대장장이처럼 손으로 칼을 만드는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Even today, there are people who make knives by hand like blacksmiths.

explain: '-장이'가 붙은 말은 손으로 물건을 만드는 기술자를 가리켜요. 일하는 곳은 '대장간'이라고 해요. 요즘은 공장에서 만들어서 이야기나 역사에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Words ending in -장이 refer to craftspeople who make things by hand. The workplace is called 대장간. Today things are made in factories, so the word appears more in stories and history.

en: send away; let someone go; see off

examples.en: Today I saw a close friend off.
I cried after sending my family off at the airport.

examples.ko: 사랑하는 사람을 떠나보내는 일은 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: Letting a loved one go is really hard.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 키운 강아지를 떠나보낸 뒤 많이 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried a lot after losing the puppy I raised for years.
It's not easy to let go of an ex.
I came on a trip to let go of the pain of the past.

explain: '보내다'는 사람이나 물건을 어디로 가게 하는 가벼운 말이고, '떠나보내다'는 가까운 사람과 헤어지거나 마음속에서 정리할 때 써서 감정이 더 커요. 세상을 떠난 사람이나 반려동물에게도 쓰고, 아픔 같은 마음을 놓아 줄 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: 보내다 is a light word for making a person or thing go somewhere. 떠나보내다 carries more emotion, used for parting from someone close or settling something in your heart. It is also used for people or pets who have died, and figuratively for letting go of pain.

examples.en: We put a period at the end of a sentence.

examples.ko: 마침표 하나를 빼먹어서 선생님이 고쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: I forgot one period, and my teacher corrected it.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 마침표가 없으면 어색해 보여요.
examples.en: A sentence without a period at the end looks awkward.
A period is a small dot, so it's easy to miss.

examples.ko: 마침표 대신 느낌표를 쓰는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: Many people use an exclamation mark instead of a period.
A period and a comma are used in different places.

explain: '온점'이라고도 하고, 쉼표(,)·물음표(?)·느낌표(!)와 같은 문장 부호예요. 공식적인 글에서는 꼭 쓰지만, 메신저에서는 안 쓰는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: I decided to put an end to the long fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 이어진 일이나 관계를 끝낼 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for ending a long-running matter or relationship.
phrases.en_equiv: put an end to; draw a line under

explain_en: It is also called 온점, and it is a punctuation mark like the comma, question mark, and exclamation mark. It is a must in formal writing, but many people skip it in messengers.

examples.en: An outlaw showed up in the town.

examples.ko: 서부 영화의 무법자는 총을 잘 쏴요.
examples.en: The outlaw in a western is a good shot.

examples.ko: 그는 규칙을 안 지켜서 동네 무법자로 불렸어요.
examples.en: He didn't follow rules, so he was called the neighborhood outlaw.
Outlaws roamed the city as they pleased.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 무법자를 주인공으로 영화를 찍었어요.
examples.en: That director made a film with an outlaw as the main character.

examples.ko: 도로 위의 무법자가 되지 않도록 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm careful not to become an outlaw on the road.

explain: '범죄자'와 비슷해 보이지만 달라요. 무법자는 법이 힘을 못 쓰는 곳에서 제멋대로 사는 사람이에요. 영화와 소설에 자주 나오고, '도로 위의 무법자'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It looks similar to 범죄자 but differs. A 무법자 lives as he pleases where the law has no power. It appears in films and novels, and also figuratively as in 도로 위의 무법자.

en: rub off and be smeared on; come off on; show through

examples.en: I touched the wall and paint rubbed off on my hand.

examples.ko: 검은 가방 색이 청바지에 묻어나서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because the black bag's color rubbed off on my jeans.
Warmth comes through in the way he speaks.
She sang in a voice that carried sadness.

examples.ko: 빨래할 때 색이 묻어나지 않게 따로 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash them separately so the color doesn't run onto others.
It's a painting that shows traces of long effort.

explain: 묻은 것이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때도 쓰고, 말투·글·표정에서 마음이나 분위기가 느껴질 때도 써요. 앞의 뜻은 '묻다'(물감이 묻다)와 가깝고, 뒤의 뜻은 '배어나다', '드러나다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is used when something sticky or colored transfers onto another surface, and also when feeling or mood comes through in speech, writing, or expression. The first sense is close to 묻다 as in 물감이 묻다, and the second is similar to 배어나다 and 드러나다.

en: fine (monetary penalty imposed as a sentence)

examples.en: He was fined and released.
It was a minor accident, so it ended with a fine.
I saw news that the court ordered a fine.

examples.ko: 잘못이 크지 않으면 벌금형에 그칠 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If the wrong isn't serious, it may end with a fine.

examples.ko: 벌금형 처분을 받은 사람은 기한 안에 돈을 내야 해요.
examples.en: A person given a fine must pay within the deadline.
A fine is generally lighter than a prison sentence.

explain: '벌금'은 내야 하는 돈이고, '벌금형'은 법원이 판결로 정한 벌을 말해요. 감옥에 가는 '징역형'과 비교해서 자주 써요. 교통 위반처럼 가벼운 일에는 '범칙금'이나 '과태료'라는 말을 써요.
explain_en: 벌금 is the money to be paid, while 벌금형 is the punishment a court decides in its ruling. It is often compared with 징역형, which means going to prison. For light matters like traffic violations, the words 범칙금 and 과태료 are used.

examples.en: The frame was crooked, so I hung it again.
The handwriting is too crooked.

examples.ko: 자 없이 그어서 선이 비뚤게 그려졌어요.
examples.en: I drew without a ruler, so the line came out crooked.

examples.ko: 비뚤던 책상 줄을 선생님이 다시 맞췄어요.
examples.en: The teacher realigned the crooked row of desks.

examples.ko: 저 탑이 조금 비뚤다고 느껴지지 않나요?
examples.en: Doesn't that tower seem a little tilted?

examples.ko: 사진이 비뚤어 보여서 각도를 다시 맞췄어요.
examples.en: The photo looked tilted, so I adjusted the angle.

explain: 실생활에서는 '비뚤어지다'를 더 많이 말해요. '마음이 비뚤어지다'는 삐딱한 태도를 비유해요. 반대말은 '반듯하다'와 '곧다'예요.
explain_en: In real life, people say 비뚤어지다 more often. 마음이 비뚤어지다 figuratively describes a warped attitude. The opposites are 반듯하다 and 곧다.

en: morning star (Venus at dawn); rising star

examples.en: I saw the morning star in the dawn sky for the first time.
I made a wish on that morning star.

examples.ko: 그 신인 선수는 야구계의 샛별로 불려요.
examples.en: That rookie is called a rising star in baseball.

examples.ko: 샛별은 해가 뜨기 직전에 가장 밝아 보여요.
examples.en: The morning star looks brightest just before sunrise.
She was a child who smiled brightly like the morning star.
At dawn the morning star set and the sun came up.

explain: 새벽 동쪽 하늘에 보이는 밝은 별(금성)이에요. 저녁 서쪽 하늘에서 보일 때는 '개밥바라기'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: That singer is a rising star of the K-pop scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나타나서 앞날이 기대되는 사람에게 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for a newcomer with a promising future.

explain_en: It is the bright star (Venus) seen in the eastern sky at dawn. When it appears in the western sky in the evening, it is called 개밥바라기.

examples.en: I put on cream right after washing my face.
I wash my face in the morning with lukewarm water.
My skin got better after I changed my cleanser.
When I finish washing my face, I dry it with a soft towel.
Skin care starts with proper face washing.
When I travel, I keep my face washing simple.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '세수'를 훨씬 자주 말해요. '세안'은 화장품 광고나 피부 관리 이야기에서 나와요. 그래서 '세안제', '클렌징'과 같이 쓰이는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In daily conversation, people say 세수 much more often. 세안 appears in cosmetics ads and skin-care talk, so it often goes with words like 세안제 and 클렌징.

examples.en: I always wash my face before bed in the evening.
Washing your face with lukewarm water is good for your skin.
After removing makeup, I washed my face slowly.

examples.ko: 아침에 세안하는 데 오 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about five minutes to wash my face in the morning.
Even when tired, you must wash your face for clean skin.
I was too sleepy yesterday and couldn't wash my face.

explain: '세수하다'가 훨씬 자연스러운 일상어예요. 화장을 지우고 닦는 것까지 말할 때는 '세안하다'를 쓰고, 얼굴에만 써요. 몸 전체는 '샤워하다', '씻다'를 써요.
explain_en: 세수하다 is the far more natural everyday word. 세안하다 is used when talking about cleansing off makeup, and only for the face. For the whole body, use 샤워하다 or 씻다.

examples.ko: 우리 반 악동이 또 장난을 쳤어요.
examples.en: The rascal of our class played a prank again.
That child is a famous troublemaker in the neighborhood.
The rascals popped balloons and ran away.
When I was little, I was called a rascal.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무대 위에서 악동 같은 모습을 보여요.
examples.en: That singer shows a bad-boy side on stage.
A cartoon starring a troublemaker is popular.

explain: '개구쟁이'는 귀엽게 장난치는 아이이고, '악동'은 말썽이 더 큰 느낌이에요. 가수나 운동선수의 이미지를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: 개구쟁이 is a kid who plays pranks in a cute way, while 악동 feels like more trouble. It is also used for the image of singers or athletes.

examples.en: As the economy worsened, employees' sense of crisis grew.

examples.ko: 저는 시험 전날이 되자 위기감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: On the day before the exam, I felt a sense of crisis.

examples.ko: 회사는 위기감 속에서 새 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The company made a new plan amid a sense of crisis.
A sense of crisis sometimes gets people moving.
Driven by a sense of crisis, I studied all night.
That sense of crisis made the team stronger.

explain: '-감'이 붙으면 상황이 아니라 그 느낌을 말해요. '위기'는 위험한 상황이고 '위기감'은 그 느낌이에요. '위기감을 느끼다', '위기감이 커지다'처럼 쓰고, '긴장감', '불안감'도 같은 방식이에요.
explain_en: Adding -감 turns a situation into the feeling about it. 위기 is the dangerous situation, and 위기감 is the feeling of it. It goes with 위기감을 느끼다 and 위기감이 커지다, and 긴장감 and 불안감 work the same way.

examples.ko: 길 앞에서 개를 보고 잠깐 주춤했어요.
examples.en: I saw a dog in front of me and paused for a moment.

examples.ko: 갑자기 소리가 나서 아이가 주춤하며 뒤를 봤어요.
examples.en: A sudden sound made the child flinch and look back.
The popularity slowed for a while and then rose again.
It was a month when sales slowed because of the rain.

examples.ko: 그는 문 앞에서 주춤해서 들어가지 못했어요.
examples.en: He hesitated at the door and couldn't go in.

examples.ko: 주춤하지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't hold back; say what you want to say.

explain: 사람이 놀라거나 망설여서 몸이 잠깐 멈출 때 쓰고, 오르던 숫자나 인기가 잠시 멈출 때도 써요. 완전히 멈추는 게 아니라 잠깐이에요. '망설이다'는 마음이 정해지지 않는 것이고, '주춤하다'는 몸이나 흐름이 잠깐 멈추는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a person stops for a moment out of surprise or hesitation, and when rising numbers or popularity pause briefly. It is not a full stop, just a short one. 망설이다 is about being undecided in your mind, while 주춤하다 is a body or trend pausing for a moment.

examples.ko: 좋은 팀에는 지도력 있는 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: A good team needs someone with leadership.
He has outstanding leadership, so everyone follows him.

examples.ko: 학급 회장은 지도력을 키우는 좋은 경험이에요.
examples.en: Being class president is a good experience for building leadership.
The boss earned the employees' trust through his leadership.
Leadership doesn't come just from speaking well.

examples.ko: 선수들은 새 감독의 지도력에 믿음이 있어요.
examples.en: The players trust the new coach's leadership.

explain: '리더십'이라고 더 자주 말해요. '지도력'은 신문이나 공식적인 글에서 많이 쓰고, '지도력이 있다/없다', '지도력을 발휘하다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '리더십'이 더 가볍게 들려요.
explain_en: People often say 리더십 instead. 지도력 is used more in newspapers and formal writing, in forms like 지도력이 있다/없다 and 지도력을 발휘하다. In everyday talk, 리더십 sounds lighter.

examples.ko: 이 강에는 작은 지류가 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: This river has several small tributaries.
A tributary flows into a big river.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 지류의 물이 먼저 불어요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the water in the tributaries rises first.
Find the tributaries of the Han River on the map.

examples.ko: 마을은 두 지류가 만나는 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: The village is where two tributaries meet.
In this tributary, water flows only in summer.

explain: 반대말은 '본류'예요. 큰 강으로 흘러 들어가는 작은 물줄기이고, 같은 말로 '지천'도 써요. 일상 대화보다 지리 수업이나 지도 설명에서 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is 본류. It is a small stream that flows into a bigger river, and 지천 means the same. It comes up in geography lessons and map descriptions more than in daily talk.

examples.en: Mom flipped the meat with tongs.

examples.ko: 게가 큰 집게발로 제 손가락을 꽉 물었어요.
examples.en: The crab pinched my finger hard with its big claw.
I clipped the laundry onto the line with clothespins.
There were no tongs, so I picked up the kimchi by hand.
At the restaurant, I held tongs and grilled meat.

examples.ko: 이 집게는 힘이 세서 잘 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: This clip is strong, so it doesn't fall off easily.

explain: '빨래집게', '머리 집게'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요. 게의 큰 발은 '집게발'이라고 해요. 아주 작은 것을 집는 도구는 '핀셋'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It often takes a word in front, as in 빨래집게 and 머리 집게. A crab's big claw is called 집게발. A tool for gripping very small things is called 핀셋.

examples.en: The intestines are several meters long.

examples.ko: 먹은 음식은 위를 지나 창자에 도착해요.
examples.en: Food passes through the stomach and arrives at the intestines.

examples.ko: 소의 창자로 만든 요리를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a dish made from cow intestines.
The intestines absorb nutrients from digested food.

examples.ko: 배가 아파서 창자 쪽이 꼬이는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt, and it felt like my insides were twisting.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 창자 검사를 받으라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to get my intestines examined.

explain: '장'은 병원이나 건강 이야기에서, '창자'는 일상 대화나 음식 이야기에서 많이 써요. 작은창자는 '소장', 큰창자는 '대장'이라고 해요. '창자가 끊어지다'처럼 슬픔을 아주 강하게 말하는 표현에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 아들을 잃은 어머니는 창자가 끊어질 듯 울었어요.
phrases.en: The mother who lost her son cried as if her heart were breaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견디기 힘든 슬픔이나 아픔을 아주 강하게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very strong way to express unbearable sorrow or pain.

explain_en: 장 is used more in hospitals and health topics, while 창자 is used more in everyday talk and food topics. The small intestine is 소장 and the large intestine is 대장. 창자 also appears in strong expressions of grief such as 창자가 끊어지다.

examples.en: On the weekend, I went to an observatory with my family.

examples.ko: 큰 망원경이 있는 천문대로 소풍을 갔어요.
examples.en: We went on a trip to an observatory with a big telescope.

examples.ko: 산 위 천문대는 별이 잘 보여서 인기예요.
examples.en: The observatory on the mountain is popular because the stars are clear.
An observatory staff member explained the constellations.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 천문대에서 일하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to work at an observatory since I was little.
When the observatory roof opens, you can see the sky.

explain: '과학관'은 전시를 보는 곳이고 '천문대'는 망원경으로 실제 하늘을 보는 곳이에요. 비슷한 말로 '관측소'가 있지만 일상에서는 '천문대'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '천문대에 가다', '천문대를 견학하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A '과학관' is a place to see exhibits, while a '천문대' is where you view the real sky through a telescope. A similar word is '관측소', but in daily life '천문대' is far more common. People say '천문대에 가다' or '천문대를 견학하다'.

examples.en: I made a flower shape with wire.
The wire is bent, so it's hard to straighten.
We put up a wire fence in the garden.
I put on gloves and held the wire carefully.
My clothes tore after catching on a wire.
This wire is thin, so it breaks easily.

explain: '전선'은 전기가 흐르는 줄이고, '철사'는 모양을 잡거나 묶을 때 쓰는 금속 줄이에요. 꽃가게나 만들기 수업에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 전선 is a cable that carries electricity, while 철사 is a metal wire used to shape or tie things. It is often used in flower shops and craft classes.

examples.en: There is a log cabin in the forest.
The children sat on a log and rested.
We cut the log and used it as firewood.
A log was floating on the river.
At the campsite, I sat on a chair made of logs.
A log is heavy and hard to move alone.

explain: '통나무집', '통나무 의자'처럼 많이 써요. '나무'는 식물이나 재료 전체를 말하지만, '통나무'는 가지를 치고 켜지 않은 둥근 나무 몸통이에요. 자른 나무판은 '널빤지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is common in compounds like 통나무집 and 통나무 의자. 나무 covers the plant or material in general, while 통나무 is a round trunk with branches removed and not yet sawn. A cut wooden board is called 널빤지.

examples.en: I put smoked salmon in the salad.
Dad bought smoked duck.
This shop has a good smoky aroma.

examples.ko: 훈제로 만든 고기는 오래 보관할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Smoked meat can be stored for a long time.

examples.ko: 훈제 맛이 강해서 아이는 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: The smoked flavor is strong, so the child doesn't eat it much.
I like raw salmon more than smoked.

explain: 음식 이름 앞에 붙여서 '훈제 오리', '훈제 연어', '훈제 치킨'처럼 말해요. 연기로 맛을 낸 음식이라서 '구이', '튀김'과 요리 방법이 달라요. 포장에 '훈제'라고만 쓰여 있는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It goes in front of a food name, as in 훈제 오리, 훈제 연어, and 훈제 치킨. The food is flavored with smoke, so the cooking method differs from 구이 or 튀김. Packages often say just 훈제.

examples.en: The ancient history lesson started in history class.
Ancient history is hard but fun.
There is still much unknown in ancient history.

examples.ko: 고대사를 공부하려면 옛 기록을 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To study ancient history, you have to read old records.
My younger sibling is very interested in ancient history.
That scholar studies the secrets of ancient history.

explain: 한국사에서 '고대'는 보통 삼국 시대와 통일신라 무렵까지를 말해요. '중세사', '근대사', '현대사'와 나란히 시대를 나눌 때 써요. 학교 역사 수업과 교과서에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In Korean history, 고대 usually means up to the Three Kingdoms and Unified Silla period. It is used alongside 중세사, 근대사, and 현대사 when dividing eras. It appears often in school history classes and textbooks.

examples.en: I smiled and said peekaboo to the baby.

examples.ko: 엄마가 얼굴을 가렸다가 까꿍 하자 아기가 웃었어요.
examples.en: When Mom covered her face and said peekaboo, the baby laughed.
The baby giggled at the peekaboo sound.
I played peekaboo with the baby for a long time.
She was hiding and then appeared saying peekaboo.
The first word the child learned is peekaboo.

explain: 아기와 얼굴을 가렸다 보여 주는 놀이를 할 때 해요. 그 놀이는 '까꿍 놀이'라고 불러요. 어른끼리는 장난으로만 써요.
explain_en: You say it when playing the game of covering and revealing your face to a baby. That game is called 까꿍 놀이. Between adults, it is used only as a joke.

examples.en: I met the final boss in the last stage of the game.
You need a lot of practice to reach the final stage.

examples.ko: 축구 경기 끝판에 골이 두 개나 나왔어요.
examples.en: Two goals came in the final stretch of the soccer game.
As the end drew near, everyone got nervous.
The last stage is always the hardest.
I felt great after clearing the last stage.

explain: 경기, 게임, 일에서 마지막 단계나 마지막 무렵을 가리켜요. '마지막'보다 입말에 가깝고 가벼워요. 비슷한 '막판'은 승부가 갈리는 마지막 순간에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The final boss of this game is really strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임의 마지막 적을 말하고, 어떤 분야에서 가장 센 것을 비유하기도 해요. 예: 매운맛의 끝판왕.
phrases.nuance_en: The last enemy in a game; also figuratively the ultimate in some field, as in the final boss of spicy food.

explain_en: It refers to the last stage or last stretch of a match, game, or task. It is more spoken and casual than 마지막. The similar 막판 fits better for the final moment when a result is decided.

examples.ko: 당분이 많은 음료는 이를 상하게 해요.
examples.en: Drinks high in sugar damage your teeth.

examples.ko: 저는 당분을 줄이려고 과일 주스를 안 마셔요.
examples.en: I don't drink fruit juice to cut down on sugar.

examples.ko: 과일에는 당분 함량이 높은 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Some fruits have a high sugar content.

examples.ko: 당분은 운동 전에 에너지를 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Sugar can give you energy before exercise.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 당분 때문에 너무 달아요.
examples.en: This snack is too sweet because of the sugar.

examples.ko: 당분이 든 간식은 한꺼번에 많이 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't eat a lot of snacks containing sugar at once.

explain: '설탕'은 요리에 넣는 하얀 가루이고, '당분'은 음식 속에 든 단 성분이에요. 그래서 '설탕을 넣다'는 되지만 '당분을 넣다'는 어색해요. 건강 이야기에서 '당분을 줄이다'를 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 설탕 is the white powder you add when cooking, while 당분 is the sweet component inside food. So 설탕을 넣다 works, but 당분을 넣다 sounds odd. In health talk, 당분을 줄이다 is common.

examples.en: I went to the bank to claim my lottery winnings.
The prize was so big that I couldn't believe it.

examples.ko: 친구가 당첨금으로 부모님께 집을 사 드렸어요.
examples.en: My friend bought his parents a house with his winnings.
I found out that tax is charged on winnings.
Be sure to check the payout date for the winnings.
I received a hundred thousand won in prize money at the event.

explain: '상금'은 대회에서 이겨서 받는 돈이고, '당첨금'은 복권이나 추첨에 뽑혀서 받는 돈이에요. 받는 방법이 달라서 말이 달라요. 복권은 '1등 당첨금'처럼 등수와 함께 말해요.
explain_en: 상금 is money you receive for winning a contest, while 당첨금 is money you receive by being drawn in a lottery or raffle. The words differ because the way of winning differs. Lotteries use forms like 1등 당첨금, with the rank.
